correctness.rationale: Exact edge-plane interpolation gives the 2+2 diagonal formulas. The 1+3 chamber obeys sum(1/t_i)=4 and Cauchy gives diameter at least 3sqrt(2)/2. Thus only the six oriented coordinate axes attain the minimum 2. The only diameter-maximal sections contain an original tetrahedron edge, yielding twelve oriented normals and endpoint 2sqrt(2). Normal-coordinate expansions give L-2=max(y^2,z^2)+O(r^4) at minima and 2sqrt(2)-L=|x+sqrt(2)y|+|x-sqrt(2)y|+O(r^2) at maxima. The latter expansion includes an explicit comparison against the extra AB-crossing vertex in the 2+2 chamber. Uniform spherical area and the Jacobian (1+r^2)^(-3/2) imply coefficients 6/pi and 3/(pi sqrt(2)). The independent package checker passed rational diagonal identities, global endpoint tests, near-max vertex-pair checks, and local spherical-area numerical consistency. Finite checks supplement rather than prove limits.

originality.rationale: Semantic searches of published published-finding corpus findings, local own-claim comparison, and primary literature searches found different observables (centrally symmetric octahedron/crosspolytope diameters, regular simplex section volumes, tetrahedron section centroid conditions and shadow moments). Inspected mathematical statements do not imply exact endpoint probabilities for tetrahedral central-section diameters, whose local nonsymmetry is essential. The motivating 2026 preprint abstract describes general probabilistic diameter bounds and p-ellipsoids, while the full paper was inaccessible; this is an explicitly retained priority risk rather than a whole-document negative assertion.

value.rationale: The natural diameter distribution of Haar-random centroidal cuts through the canonical noncentrally symmetric Platonic solid has two fully classified extrema, rigorously distinct sharp tail exponents, exact leading constants, and square-versus-rectangle conditional direction profiles. These quantitative rare-event benchmarks sharpen general estimates for random convex-section diameters and distinguish local quadratic stability from an edge-support cusp. They are mathematically motivated by the underlying complete tetrahedral section geometry, not by an arbitrary small finite parameter experiment.
